card.name: Linking words before electrolyte disturbances
card.fires_on: Small linking words or punctuation (of, and, comma, e.g.) right before an expected electrolyte or fluid-imbalance term such as hypokalemia, hyponatremia, or potassium. Found in warnings about fluids, dehydration and serum sodium or potassium.

modes.label: Before electrolyte terms
modes.description: A link word after a fluid or electrolyte problem, where another electrolyte condition is likely to follow.
modes.example: close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium levels to avoid hypoglycemia<< and>> hypok

modes.label: Within dehydration and fluid warnings
modes.description: A link word or comma inside a list of signs of dehydration, fluid overload or sodium imbalance.
modes.example: excessive fluid absorption and permanent morbidity or death as a result of hyponatremia<<,>> hypoosmolality and/or fluid overload

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like potassium and sodium, and Chinese terms for them.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words when the text is about to name a salt or fluid imbalance such as low potassium or sodium.
